title: Amos White brings him to the New Orleans Jazz Club
summary: Amos White invited him to a boat session and he returned to traditional jazz.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, I guess a few years ago, you somehow decided to go over to the New Orleans Jazz Club here in San Francisco. You really hadn't been too much in contact with that scene here, the kind of traditional jazz scene. Even though there were a lot of traditional players around San Francisco, Pops Foster and Darnell Howard. But about five or six years ago, suddenly you went back and started playing traditional jazz. How did that happen?
Amos White. Amos White invited me to one of the sessions.
He was a trumpet player.
He was a trumpet player.
He was what, in his 80s then? Wonderful person.
Yes, yes. He was, I think he died in his 90s when he was 90-some years old.
He was famous for playing the trumpet breaks in Fade Marable's record of Frankie and Johnny, I believe.
Yeah, he was a good musician.
Yeah.
A wonderful person.
So what did Amos say?

Amos invited me to, first time was a boat. They had a boat excursion. No, it was not an excursion. They had the New Orleans Jazz Club had a session on the boat, one of the boats out here in San Francisco. He invited me to come out and take this boat ride. And during that time, he asked me to play a couple of tunes. I just had an operation at that time.
Yeah.
I think it was a league operation or something. I was healing in some way. So I went on that boat. That was my first time I knew anything about the New Orleans Jazz Club.
Yeah, and suddenly you heard all these old tunes from your youth again, right?
Yes, yes.
Did you play that day?

I played, I think it was a couple of tunes, not too many, because I played on Amos horn. And the second time that I attended one of these sessions is Amos, they gave Amos a plaque of some kind, an award. It was at the Claremont Hotel in Oakland. And I didn't have a horn. And that time, a guy loaned me his cornet, and Amos and I played together. We played the St. Louis Blues.
Oh, really?
That was my second time. And from then on, I've been there. I like that club very much.
